llm.summary: The skill's code, runtime instructions, and requested inputs are consistent with a SocialEcho API CLI: it only asks for an API key via CLI flags and calls the stated api.socialecho.net endpoints, with no extra credentials, unusual installs, or hidden behavior.

dimensions.detail: The name/description, SKILL.md, OpenAPI, and included JS CLIs all implement SocialEcho API operations (team, account, article, report, upload URL, reddit/pinterest listing, publish). There are no unrelated credentials, binaries, or services requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs using CLI options (--api-key, --base-url, --team-id, etc.) and not auto-reading env vars; the JS files require the same CLI flags and only read local payload/docs files when explicitly asked (publish payload and platform limits). Network calls go only to the configured baseUrl (default https://api.socialecho.net). There is no instruction to read unrelated system files or transmit arbitrary local data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided and package.json lists no dependencies. The repo is runnable with Node >=18 and npm ci, but there are no downloads from untrusted URLs or extract steps. No risky install behavior detected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare environment variables or primary credentials. It requires a team API key supplied via CLI (--api-key) at runtime, which matches the described purpose. No unrelated secrets or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false, agent invocation is normal, and the skill does not request persistent system-wide changes or modify other skills/config. It only runs as a CLI helper and does not attempt to persist credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears coherent with its SocialEcho API purpose. Before using it: 1) Inspect the included JS files (they are small and readable) and verify you trust the source; 2) Only provide API keys created for the intended SocialEcho team (do not reuse unrelated high-privilege keys); 3) When overriding --base-url, avoid pointing it at unknown hosts (an attacker-controlled base URL would receive your API key and payloads); 4) Review any publish payload JSON before calling publish-article to avoid accidental posting; 5) Run the code in an isolated environment if you are unsure (it requires Node >=18 and has no runtime dependencies).
